# Flat vs. Projectively Flat Connections

## Flat Connections

A connection $\nabla$ is **flat** if its curvature vanishes identically:

$$R^\nabla = 0$$

This means parallel transport is path-independent (depends only on the homotopy class of the path). Equivalently, there exist local frames in which the connection coefficients vanish entirely. Flat connections correspond to locally trivial bundles with structure determined purely by holonomy (monodromy) representations.

## Projectively Flat Connections

A connection $\nabla$ on a manifold is **projectively flat** if it is *projectively equivalent* to a flat connection. Two connections $\nabla$ and $\bar{\nabla}$ are **projectively equivalent** if they have the same geodesics *as unparameterized curves*, meaning:

$$\bar{\nabla}_X Y = \nabla_X Y + \phi(X)Y + \phi(Y)X$$

for some 1-form $\phi$. So a projectively flat connection may have nonzero curvature, but its geodesics can be reparameterized to match those of a flat connection (i.e., they are "straight lines" in local affine coordinates, up to reparameterization).

## Key Differences

| | Flat | Projectively Flat |
|---|---|---|
| **Curvature** | $R = 0$ | $R \neq 0$ in general |
| **Geodesics** | Straight lines in local coordinates | Straight lines up to reparameterization |
| **Obstruction** | Curvature tensor | **Projective Weyl tensor** (the projectively invariant part of curvature) |
| **Characterization** | Vanishing of $R$ | Vanishing of the projective curvature tensor $W$ |

## The Precise Condition

For an affine connection on an $n$-dimensional manifold ($n \geq 2$), projective flatness is characterized by the vanishing of the **projective Weyl tensor**. In dimension $n \geq 3$, this is the trace-free part of the curvature under the projective equivalence class. In dimension $n = 2$, every connection is projectively Weyl-flat, and projective flatness requires a separate condition involving derivatives of the projective Schouten tensor.

## Example

The **Levi-Civita connection of the round sphere** $S^n$ is projectively flat (its geodesics are great circles, which correspond to straight lines under gnomonic projection) but is certainly **not flat** (the sphere has nonzero curvature). More generally, any constant-sectional-curvature Riemannian manifold has a projectively flat Levi-Civita connection.

## Summary

Every flat connection is projectively flat, but not conversely. Projective flatness is a strictly weaker condition that forgets the "affine parameterization" information and only asks whether the geodesic paths themselves look like straight lines.
